# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Convert emission exceedance values to the appropriate mass units (i.e., non-methane hydrocarbon [NMHC] readings to kilograms per hour, etc.).
3. Calculate the total amount emissions released for the exceedance.
4. Convert total emission release amounts to tons.
5. Use the air pollution coefficients from the Alberta air emission inventory manual ([here](http://www.aeri.ca/Alberta%20Air%20Emissions%20Inventory%20Manual%202014.pdf)).
6. Calculate the air quality impact.


# How to convert emissions exceedance values to the appropriate mass units: sulfur oxides (SOx) & particulate matter (PM) concentration measurements are reported in parts per million (ppm); non-methane hydrocarbon (NMHC) readings are reported in ppbv; ammonia concentration readings are reported in micrograms per cubic metre (ug/m3).
